title: Implementing map, filter, and flatten from scratch
hook: FAANG interviews ask you to polyfill Array.prototype.map without using map — same pattern for filter, flatten, and flatMap. You must know index, thisArg, sparse arrays, and mutation rules.

blocks.text: Implementing **map** means new array, loop indices 0..length-1, skip holes or include per spec, call callback `(element, index, array)`, push result. **filter** pushes when callback truthy. **flatten** recursively or iteratively expands nested arrays to depth. **flatMap** is map then flat(1) — one pass optimization in native code. Respect **length** property even if sparse — do not use for...of alone if holes matter.

entries.plainDefinition: Userland implementation of built-in missing in older engines.
Predicate or mapper invoked per index with element, index, whole array.
Optional value bound as this inside callback — map/filter support it.
How many nesting levels to flatten — Infinity for full flatten.

blocks.text: Implement-from-scratch proves you understand iteration, not just API names. Same skills build **custom collections**, **Observable** operators, and **ORM** mappers. C# **Select** extension method is similar — LINQ to Objects is lazy IEnumerable, your JS polyfill is eager array.

blocks.title: Interview trap: mutate during iteration
blocks.body: Spec: length may change during map/filter — use careful index loop. Mention this for senior credit.

snippet.label: map from scratch
snippet.explanation: >>> 0 converts length to uint32 like spec. k in O preserves holes in result.

snippet.label: filter from scratch
snippet.explanation: Result length unknown — push instead of pre-sized array. Truthy predicate like native filter.

snippet.label: flatten recursive
snippet.explanation: Interview follow-up: iterative stack version avoids recursion depth limit on huge nesting.

snippet.label: Failure mode: using for...of on sparse array
snippet.explanation: Polyfill must match spec index iteration, not iterator skipping holes.

blocks.title: Pitfalls to avoid
blocks.body: for...of polyfill losing sparse slots. Forgetting callback TypeError. flat recursive stack overflow on deep nest — use iterative. Mutating input array inside map while iterating.

blocks.text: Extend interview: **flatMap** one-pass, **reduce** polyfill, **Array.from** with mapFn. Discuss spec vs simple version — when interview wants spec-accurate vs 'works for dense arrays'. In production use native methods — polyfills for education and legacy only.

blocks.title: What gets you rejected in interviews
blocks.body: Cannot write map in 5 minutes. Using result.push in map without understanding pre-sized array spec. No mention of callback thisArg or holes.

interviewTakeaways: map polyfill: index loop 0..length, k in array, callback.call(thisArg).
filter pushes when predicate truthy — result length dynamic.
flat: recursive or stack; flatMap = map + flat(1) = SelectMany.
60s: Implement map/filter with length >>> 0 and k in O. Holes matter. flat recursive depth. C# Select lazy; JS eager. thisArg optional.
Follow-up: iterative flatten without recursion stack overflow.
commonPitfalls: for...of polyfill that skips sparse holes incorrectly for map spec.
filter/map without validating callback is function.
Strong answer: write map from scratch, explain holes, thisArg, flat depth, SelectMany parallel.

jsTsCorrelations.note: Implementations often generic <T, U> for mapper — mirrors writing Select<T,R> in C#.
arguments and DOM NodeList have length — polyfill uses Object(array) pattern like Array.prototype methods.
